subject: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps — Acme Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-12T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap & proposed dedicated capacity for Acme Health

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re all aligned and so I can get the SOW and pricing over to your procurement team. TL;DR: Acme needs predictable, isolated inference capacity for patient-facing features with strict data isolation, 24/7 availability, and clear unit economics.

Pain points you called out:
- Intermittent latency spikes during morning peaks (8–10am ET) impacting user experience
- Rising per-token costs and unpredictable spend due to bursty traffic
- Regulatory requirement to keep PHI in a customer-owned VPC and strict auditability

Goals / success criteria:
- Reserved (dedicated) capacity with VPC isolation and KMS integration
- SLA: 99.9% uptime, p50 latency < 150ms for typical requests, p95 < 400ms
- Autoscaling buffer for predictable peak handling; predictable monthly billing

Proposed initial configuration (price/terms will be in SOW):
- Dedicated pool: 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved) with support for vertical/horizontal scaling
- Private deployment: customer VPC peering + KMS/HSM support for keys
- Autoscale policy: maintain baseline throughput for steady traffic + 25% burst headroom; rapid fallback to smaller model variant on contention
- Technical support: 24/7 on-call and monthly performance reviews

Next steps / asks:
1) I’ll send a draft SOW + pricing spreadsheet to procurement by EOD tomorrow (attached).
2) Rishi — can we schedule a 60-min deep-dive to validate the sizing assumptions and confirm the KV-cache/autoscale behavior? Ideally this week.
3) Jordan — can you confirm expected sustained qps and peak qps (approx numbers) and procurement timeline (PO vs. contract cadence)?
4) You asked about a pilot — we can do a timeboxed pilot on a smaller reserved pool (4 GPUs) with credits applied; I’ll include options in the SOW.

Attaching: initial SOW template and pricing workbook (will iterate based on the SE call).

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132
From: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-12T17:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & proposed dedicated capacity for Acme Health

Marissa —

Thanks for the concise recap. That aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:

- Data isolation is non-negotiable for our legal/compliance teams. Any solution must live in our VPC with customer-managed keys and detailed audit logs for all inference requests.
- Expected traffic: sustained baseline ~40 qps, peak up to ~220 qps during morning surge (15–30 minute bursts).
- Pilot: procurement prefers a 2–4 week technical pilot before committing. We’d want logs, monitoring, and a small subset of production traffic routed.
- Procurement timeline: target PO by mid-November if the pilot looks good.

On the SLA numbers: 99.9% sounds reasonable; can you confirm how Redwood measures availability (region-level vs. pool-level) and what credits look like if missed? Also please include estimated token/unit costs for baseline vs. burst.

I’ll loop in procurement (procurement@acmehealth.com) for the SOW review once you send it.

Best,
Jordan

Hi Jordan — quick technical follow-up from our side.

We can support the isolation and throughput requirements you described. A few notes:
- Sizing: 8 A100-equivalent GPUs should provide steady-state throughput for ~40 qps with headroom for 220 qps bursts if we enable burst autoscaling and prefix/KV caching. If your models have very long context windows we should account for higher memory usage; please share typical prompt + response sizes.
- VPC & keys: We’ll deploy the runtime in a private tenant with VPC peering, and we support both customer-managed KMS and HSM-backed keys for encryption at rest.
- Autoscale behavior: baseline pool + reactive scale for queued requests. For burst protection we can configure warm standby shards to reduce cold-start latency.
- Pilot: Recommend 2-week pilot on 4 GPUs (same VPC/KMS setup) with full telemetry. We’ll capture traces, token-level cost, and latency slices so procurement/engineering can validate.

I attached a quick tech appendix and the initial SOW draft. I’ve also added links to our runbook for audit logs and the SLA doc.

Proposed SE call windows: Oct 13 09:00–11:00 PT or Oct 14 14:00–16:00 PT. Which works for you?

—
Rishi Malhotra
